summary: Prefetch context eviction causes transparent route shift for enterprise tenant during canary streaming sessions
description: Issue summary: During a weighted canary in us-east-1 we observed a small cohort of streaming sessions for tenant NimbleDocs being silently routed to a compat variant (redwood-compat-1.2) despite an explicit tenant model pin. Impact: ~3% of active streams for the tenant received degraded outputs (tokenization differences) and one customer-facing workflow reported hallucination-like deltas. Environment: production (us-east-1), canary slice (10% traffic), streaming API with chunked/resume enabled. Timeline: 2026-01-25 09:12 UTC first customer alert -> 09:18 Support ticket opened -> 09:25 SRE attached initial traces -> 10:10 mitigation rollback and patch rollout completed. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and follow-ups.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a tenant session pinned to rwkv-7b-v2 and enable streaming with chunked-resume
2) Trigger a canary slice for a new model variant while shadow prewarm is active
3) Simulate a short prefetch TTL expiry by forcing a prewarm reconciliation out-of-band
4) Observe routing metadata on the edge and check whether session routing falls back to compat variant
5) Reproduce in staging with identical prewarm TTL and header normalization enabled to validate behavior.

2026-01-25T09:14:23Z orchestrator: WARN route-decide: tenant=nimble-42 pin=rwkv-7b-v2 metadata=missing -> fallback=compat-1.2
2026-01-25T09:14:24Z serving-runtime: ERROR stream: tenant=nimble-42 model=compat-1.2 token-delta=+12
comments: 2026-01-25 09:18 - Support (Ava): Customer reports intermittent content drift in streaming chat after canary cutover. They provided sample session IDs and a transcript showing tokenization mismatch.

2026-01-25 09:26 - SRE (Daniel): Initial traces show prefetch stamp expired immediately prior to session resume and the orchestrator 'route-decide' returned fallback variant. Opening orchestrator trace and edge headers capture.

2026-01-25 10:02 - Eng (Priya Rao): Edge header normalizer was trimming a trailing 'x-prefetch' attribute when prewarm TTL is zeroed during reconciliation. Patch proposed to preserve pin metadata until route commit.
2026-01-25 10:08 - CS (Liam O'Connor): NimbleDocs accepted a temporary mitigation: revert canary weight to 0% for the tenant while patch rolls out.
2026-01-25 10:23 - Daniel: Patch deployed to edge-proxy and orchestrator in us-east-1. Observed pinned sessions re-binding. Monitoring for 30 minutes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Prefetch TTL mismatch caused prefix/KV cache to be evicted on edge just before stream resume, removing routing fingerprint.
Hypothesis B: Header normalizer rewrite removed a pin header when the prefetch payload was empty; this exposed a microwindow where route selection fell back to policy-based variant selection.
Trace analysis: Orchestrator logs show route decision keys missing 'pin' attribute for the affected session IDs; edge-proxy traces show prefetch expiry events 200-600ms before the resume call.
Repro: Reproduced in staging by cycling prewarm TTL during a chunked resume; reproduced only when header normalization was enabled and prefetch reconciliation overlapped resume.

Root cause: Race between prewarm reconciliation (clearing short-lived prefetch payloads) and streaming resume logic. Header normalizer dropped empty-prefetch header which the routing layer used as a pin-safe-guard; without it orchestrator applied fallback rules leading to transparent routing to compat variant.
Risk assessment: Issue affects streaming sessions that resume across prewarm reconciliation windows; not observed on non-streaming short-lived requests.
Temporary mitigation: Scoped canary weight rollback for tenant and increased prewarm TTL for affected slice.
resolution: Patched edge-proxy header normalizer to retain pin headers when prefetch payload empty; adjusted prewarm reconciliation ordering in orchestrator and increased default prewarm TTL for streaming slices. Canary weight for NimbleDocs rolled back to 0% during patch rollout, then restored after verification.
resolution_notes: Hotfix 1 (edge-proxy) merged and deployed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/391 — preserves x-tenant-pin header when prefetch is empty.
Hotfix 2 (orchestrator) merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1228 — serialization of prewarm reconciliation before session resume decision.
Rollout: us-east-1 edge and orchestrator patch applied 10:08-10:20 UTC 2026-01-25; nimble canary weight set to 0% at 10:05 and restored to 10% at 10:40 after 30m healthy checks.

Postmortem owner: Daniel Singh. Follow-ups: implement metric for prefetch-expiry-before-resume; create alert when fallback rate for pinned tenants >0.5% over 5m, add end-to-end test in canary pipeline that simulates prewarm TTL crosses during chunked resume.
Customer communication: Support sent post-incident summary and details to NimbleDocs; they confirmed restored quality and accepted SLA credit offer for the impacted window.
